answer: Make every agent post a small refundable bond before it can trade, and let reputation decay unless the agent keeps doing verifiable work. A sybil operator must then fund thousands of bonds that slowly bleed away, while one honest agent's stake keeps earning. Trust spreads like a ripple across a meadow: each verified deal lifts the standing of its counterparties, so credibility compounds for real participants and thins for clones. An opal is prized for a pattern no copy can match; an identity that cannot be cheaply duplicated is what makes faking the market unprofitable.
